text: Offer your interlocutor the gift of your non-knowing. When someone tells you about their problem, shares a difficult story, renounce all your assessments, knowledge, advice, and “obvious solutions.” Move from the head into the heart, and become pure space of presence that will receive the interlocutor together with their story. Listen sincerely, feel, maintain the dialogue only so that the interlocutor opens up and the story unfolds. At some point your interlocutor will feel better, and the perfect solution may come to them by itself. This format of communication is far more interesting than the traditional one. The desire to give advice in many cases only increases the distance, placing people in different roles, and is a subtle form of pride. Whereas your quiet presence is a healing space of love and wisdom, in which miracles happen by themselves.
